messages:
incident-bot: Paging maya (on-call). Runtime pod rti-serve-44 on node gpu-13 repeatedly crash-looping (SIGSEGV). High error rate observed for /v1/generate; >90% requests failing for several dedicated customers. :rotating_light:

maya: ack, joining. Any initial impact numbers?

raj: I see OOMs followed by SIGSEGV in fused_kernels.cu. Logs show CUDA driver error right before the segfault. Sample from pod logs:
```
[2026-03-16T21:25:19Z] runtime: launching batch n=8 seq=1024
[2026-03-16T21:25:19Z] cuda: cuCtxSynchronize -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION
[2026-03-16T21:25:19Z] SIGSEGV at 0x7fff0000 in fused_attention_kernel
backtrace: fused_attention.cu:432
```

elaine: spike in restarts across three nodes (gpu-11/gpu-12/gpu-13). Kube shows CrashLoopBackOff with exit code 139. Node flaps correlated to 21:24-21:28 window.

sam: Customer A (dedicated) reporting timeouts and degraded latency. CS triage opened; they're escalated to SOC.

maya: ok immediate plan: 1) scale down prod replicas for hosted pool to reduce blast radius 2) cordon gpu-13 and drain any remaining pods 3) toggle runtime feature flag to disable TRT fused kernels 4) alert eng-runtime for hotfix.

raj: executing steps 3 and 1 now. Disabling OPT_TRT_FUSED=true -> false via configmap rollout.

deploy-bot: rollout started: configmap/runtime-optimizations -> deployment/rti-serve (3->3)

maya: running drain on gpu-13: `kubectl drain gpu-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

elaine: nodes drained. I'm moving all remaining pods off gpu-11/12 as precaution and restarting the runtime daemon on those nodes.

raj: after disabling fused kernels, we still see a few crashes but much lower rate. Looks like crash rate dropped from ~120/min to ~4/min. Kernel backtrace now shows runtime path in trt_plugin_loader instead of fused kernel. Possibly a corrupted tensor layout used by TRT op.

maya: good. For customers on Dedicated we need to: 1) start failover to compatible model variant (quantized but without TRT) 2) schedule a rolling restart for dedicated pools to pick up config change 3) open a Sev2 ticket and notify account teams. Sam can handle customer comms.

sam: on it. Notifying AEs and emailing customer A with ETA 30m and mitigation steps taken.

raj: temp mitigation that helped on one host: set env `ALLOCATOR_MAX_ACTIVE_BYTES=0.8` and restart pod. That reduced memory footprint and avoided the immediate illegal instruction in that run. We'll need a proper patch.

maya: eng-runtime, please capture core dumps and full dmesg from the affected nodes before uncordoning. Also preserve the pod images and the exact configmap commit sha.

raj: pulling cores now: `kubectl cp gpu-13:/var/crash/core.rti-serve-44 ./` and saving to /artifacts/2131415926. Collected dmesg and nvidia-smi output.

elaine: raising incident bridge for next 30m. On-call handoff scheduled at +1h. I'll create pager note for follow-up postmortem and tag reliability and runtime teams.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2131415926. Severity: Sev2. Bridge: https://meet.bridge/INC-2131415926

maya: summary for post-incident: probable root cause pilot: a TensorRT fused kernel encountering a layout mismatch under specific sequence length distribution causing illegal instruction on this driver/GPU combo -> cascade into SIGSEGV and node-level instability. Immediate mitigations: disable TRT fused kernels, cordon affected nodes, restart with lower allocator limit, failover dedicated customers to non-TRT variant. Next actions: collect full traces, reproduce in staging with same driver/TensorRT 8.6, and prepare a runtime patch or a model graph transform to avoid fused path.

sam: communicated to customers; one customer confirmed they see recovery. Will update when all are green.

maya: thanks team. keep updates in thread. leave a note if any node re-flaps.

(End of thread)
